about: Facts the certificate must keep. scripts/check_fidelity.py checks each one against facts.json, so that a change to Certificate/Facts.lean cannot quietly lose them. They answer Astra's outside review (docs/reports/outside-review-01.md), which asked for these regressions by name; brief 0005, stage 1k. Each names an entry by its ref and a field of it (Certificate/FIELDS.md), and asks that the list `includes` some names, `excludes` others, or holds exactly `count.is` names beginning with `count.prefix`; `equals` compares the field with a value. A field that is an object, as `inherited` is, is read by its keys, and a field the entry lacks fails. A field that is a list of objects, as `cited_laws` is, is read by each object's `law`; with `law`, an expectation reads that cited law's `construction_rules` instead. An expectation with no `ref` reads a field of the top level of facts.json, as `construction_rules` is. One with `"every": "entry"` and no `ref` reads its field in every entry, porisms and companions included, and asks only that it `excludes` some names; there a list of objects, as `shared_steps` is, is read by each object's `name`. One with `one_of` gives an entry two states or more, each a `state` name and a list of its ordinary `expectations`, and names as its `field` the field of the entry that tells them apart, which one expectation at least of every state reads; it holds when exactly one state does, as I.4 is held, by its `own_axioms`, to Metric 9 or to Common Notion 4 for figures, and III.1 Por., by its `axioms`, to the list of either (#517). `why` is shown when one fails.

expectations.why: The porism's own entry pins every assumption of its proof by the argument of Euclid's reductio from the given centre, counted separately from III.1's construction: 38 tacit rules after the second retirement, and 38 still once Book Zero came to rest on the radius rule (#473), with radius_ne_zero in the place of circle_eq. Since Book Zero and the porism's own case of a centre on AB stopped using Circle 1 (#477), between_of_inside_chord is gone from the list and the count is 37. Since centre_unique is now a theorem, excluding its name from axioms cannot detect a call to it; the pin on the porism's proved_rules, below, can (#168). The proof neither calls III.1 nor uses exists_centre.

Once I.4's area clause rests on Common Notion 4 for figures (Tacit.figures_coincide) in the place of Metric 9 (Tacit.area_congruent), as #517 moves it, the porism reaches the new axiom through what it cites, back to I.4, where it reached Metric 9: the same 37 tacit rules, with figures_coincide in the place of area_congruent and no other name changed. As in the state "Metric 9", centre_unique is a theorem, so excluding its name from axioms cannot detect a call to it; the pin on the porism's proved_rules, below, can (#168). The proof neither calls III.1 nor uses exists_centre.

III.1 Por.'s axioms are pinned exactly, in one of two states, while #517 moves I.4's area clause from Metric 9 (Tacit.area_congruent) to Common Notion 4 for figures (Tacit.figures_coincide) and both axioms stand in the foundations: the list with Metric 9, as before the move, or the same list with the new axiom in its place. So each part of the move passes on its own, and the move's contract pins the new axiom's list alone (docs/decisions/2026-10-31-517-pin-either.md). The two lists differ, so at most one state holds; a tree whose porism rests on both axioms, or on neither, holds neither state, and fails (#517).

III.1's certificate now also carries exists_centre, for D within by III.2's argument inside its construction and for the supposed centre G of its reductio, and the entry pins it by name, so that the count alone cannot hide it giving way to another rule. It is counted separately from its porism: 39 tacit rules after the second retirement, and 38 since Book Zero and III.1's own proof stopped using Circle 1 (#477), between_of_inside_chord gone and nothing gained. Since centre_unique is now a theorem, excluding its name from axioms cannot detect a call to it; the claim that this proof avoids it rests on proof review.
A porism's entry names its proposition.

A proposition lists its porism and its companions, so that it is not complete until each is proved. III.1's one companion, Prop1.of_circle, runs III.1's construction on two points of a circle it takes itself, and proofs take the centre by it where Heath's "[III. 1]" stands (#547, #381).

III.2's own Lean does not call Circle 2 (Argon's second review; #65). Circle 2 has been a theorem since 19 October 2026, so excluding its name from own_axioms cannot detect a call to it; nor can the axioms pin's exclusion of Circle 3, a theorem too since 24 October 2026 (#294). Both are now proved after III.2, in Elements/BookIII/Prop02.lean, from its corollary Prop2.within, and a proof of III.2 cannot use a theorem proved from III.2, since Lean admits no circular proof.

No lemma that III.2 calls uses Circle 2 (#65). Circle 2 has been a theorem since 19 October 2026, so excluding its name from inherited cannot detect such a use; nor can the axioms pin's exclusion of Circle 3, a theorem too since 24 October 2026 (#294). Both are now proved after III.2, from its corollary Prop2.within, so no lemma that III.2 calls can use either: Lean admits no circular proof.
I.5's own Lean never calls Postulate 3: like Euclid's proof, it draws no circle (#65).

Postulate 3 reaches I.5's proof through Book Zero's exists_between_nearer, which keeps a point taken at random near enough with a circle; a lemma's axioms are inherited, not the proof's own (Argon's second review; #65).

This pin once checked that III.2 did not rest on Circle 3, then an axiom, and kept Circle 2's retired name out of its axiom list (#60). Circle 2 has been a theorem since 19 October 2026 and Circle 3 since 24 October (#294); both are now proved after III.2, from its corollary Prop2.within, so excluding their names from axioms can no longer fail: a theorem is in no entry's axioms. What keeps III.2 off them now is Lean: a proof of III.2 cannot use a theorem proved from III.2, since Lean admits no circular proof.

This pin holds the state #477 reached with Circle 1 (Tacit.between_of_inside_chord) still an axiom: III.2 rests on it no longer. Its own proof, when AB passes through the centre, puts the centre between A and B by Book Zero's between_of_centre_chord, from Definition I.15, Between 6 and the radius rule; and Generalities 4 (inside_not_on), through which Circle 1 reached the propositions III.2 cites, is proved without it. While Circle 1 is an axiom, the pin fails if III.2's proof, or anything it rests on, uses the rule again. Once Circle 1 is proved after III.2, as the owner's decision of 25 October 2026 provides, its name is in no entry's axioms and the pin can no longer fail; Lean then keeps III.2 off it, since it admits no circular proof.

III.1 shows the middle point of its chord within the circle by I.5, I.16 and I.19, as III.2 does, and does not rest on Circle 3 (#60). Circle 2 has been a theorem since 19 October 2026 and Circle 3 since 24 October; both are now proved after III.2 (#294), so excluding their names from axioms can no longer fail. A proof that used either would cite III.2, since the walk that finds an entry's cites passes through proved rules (the II.1 pin), and check_fidelity refuses III.1's citing III.2, which does not come before it; the pin on III.1's cites, next, can fail.

#60's claim that III.1 does not rest on Circle 3 now takes this form (#294): III.1 does not cite III.2, as a proof using Circle 2, Circle 3, Points 9 or Intersection 2 would. All four are proved after III.2 since 24 October 2026, and a proof that uses any of them cites III.2, for the walk that finds an entry's cites passes through proved rules, as the II.1 pin shows.

No proof uses Circle 2 (Tacit.inside_of_between), Circle 3 (Tacit.outside_of_between) or Intersection 2 (Tacit.line_meets_circle_of_opposite_sides), as Book III's introduction, docs/FORMALIZATION.md and docs/reports/overlaps.md say (#429). All three are proved after III.2, in Elements/BookIII/Prop02.lean, and each cites III.2 (proved_rule_cites), so an entry whose own Lean calls one, in its theorem or in a helper in its proposition's namespace, lists it among its shared steps. A call made only through another lemma lists that lemma instead, with III.2 among what it brings in, and is kept by review. Points 9 (Tacit.exists_point_outside_circle), unused too, is not pinned: no page says it is unused, and a proof after III.2 may use it.

A construction rule is an axiom whose conclusion asserts existence once the project's definitions are unfolded (docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 9): the postulates that draw, the rules that give a point, and those that conclude CirclesMeet or LinesMeet are among them. A rule that concludes an equality, a negation, OutsideCircle, an order read through its instance, or the restricted rule is not. Every rule it requires is still an axiom, and so is every rule it excludes but two: Tacit.pasch3, which the second retirement wave proves as a theorem, and Tacit.outside_of_between (Circle 3), which concludes OutsideCircle and has been a theorem since 24 October 2026, proved after III.2 (#294). A theorem is in no list of axioms, so excluding those two can no longer fail (#150, question 4).
